_comment: CONSTRAINT-AWARE GLOBAL sigma0 (docs/SPEC_prior_residual_census.md §14) -- the
DEGRADED-PATH arm.  Extends _ft63_s0g_raimlive.json and turns OFF exactly one
thing: network.raim_redundancy_normalize.
IT MUST EXTEND THE raimlive LINEAGE, NOT THE CENSUS ONE.  MEASURED 2026-08-04:
on a lineage without phase_leveling the post-fit RAIM pass is never called at
all (carry_warm = phase_leveling && warmup brackets it), so the data side sees
ZERO rows and the r == 1 fallback NEVER FIRES -- an 'approx' arm built there
would exercise the NO_DATA path and quietly test nothing about APPROX.  The
first draft of this file made that mistake; it is recorded here so the next
reader does not repeat it.
WHY AN ARM FOR A DEGRADED PATH AT ALL.  Standing invariant #4: a degraded output
must SAY SO, and the only way to know the saying-so works is to run it.  This
arm exercises, on real data:
* the loader WARN naming raim_redundancy_normalize and the DIRECTION of the
bias (Sum-r_data becomes a ROW COUNT, so the denominator is too large and
sigma0_global reads LOW -- a known direction, not an unknown error);
* the one-shot run-time WARN at the first affected epoch, with its row counts;
* the APPROX bit (value 1) in the s0g_flags column of every affected epoch;
* the run-end tally of each degradation mode.
It is also the mode most FT63-class runs will actually be in, because the
standing armed set does not include raim_redundancy_normalize -- so this is what
an ordinary reader will see, and its numbers have to be interpretable.
NOT AN A/B CONTROL.  raim_redundancy_normalize is SOLVE-AFFECTING (it changes
the RAIM residual standardization, hence which arcs refloat).  Compare
sigma0_global between this arm and _ft63_s0g_raimlive.json only to CONFIRM THE
DIRECTION of the degradation, never to quote a difference: the two solves are
not the same solve.
